solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Staff of millions given good service

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)
in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch, a very good service

explanation.surface: A worker for a huge firm, perhaps, rewarded for delivering excellent service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, but it is a ceremonial rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial rod carried as a symbol of authority, as in Parliament, is a kind of staff.

clue.text: Chance I'm terrible engineer

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful mess, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone admits that their odds of passing as an engineer are poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or machine repairer is commonly called a mechanic, a broad sense of engineer.

clue.text: Waterway in N America, in western US state

indicators.note: the second 'in' says the first piece sits inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
NA abbreviates North America

explanation.surface: Describing where in North America a waterway can be found, in a western state.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; the second is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial channel cut for boats is a man-made waterway.

clue.text: Branch not on fire

parts.note: a switch that is not on is off
to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: A tree branch that is not burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A side growth from a plant's stem, or an organisation's spin-off, is a branch.

clue.text: Visionary ruler often let broadcast

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters of these words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A far-sighted monarch who frequently allowed things to be aired.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who claims to see the future is a seer, a visionary in the prophetic sense.

clue.text: Parents' quibble, holding this firework

indicators.note: the words hold the letters inside them, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad argue about a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' hides the answer in parentS QUIBble.
explanation.definitionFit: A small firework that fizzes before going off with a bang; the source of the phrase 'damp squib'.

clue.text: Japanese art in old Baltic capital makes impact at first

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia, a Baltic state

indicators.note: applies to both following words, taking just their opening letters

explanation.surface: A Japanese art exhibition makes a splash when shown in Latvia's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper folding into shapes is a traditional craft from Japan.

clue.text: Care for fashion that queen's abandoned

indicators.note: the queen's letter has been left behind, taken out of the word for fashion

parts.note: a trend is a fashion
R, for Regina, is the queen; the 's is read as 'is' or ownership linking to the deletion

explanation.surface: The queen gives up following fashion to look after others.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a patient or garden is to look after it, to care for it.

clue.text: Top of joint on aquatic mammal's pad

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed on another sits above it
in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an otter is an aquatic mammal; the 's is read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A cut of meat on an otter's paw pad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' looks like an animal's paw, but it is a notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A small notebook for jotting notes is a writing pad.

clue.text: Study sightseeing itinerary outline

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a tour is a planned sightseeing trip

explanation.surface: Someone poring over a travel plan's broad outline.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for 'study' is an old usage common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a map or the shape of a body's edges is its outline.

clue.text: Working after university partnership

indicators.note: the word for working comes after the university piece

parts.note: uni is the informal British word for university
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A partnership formed once one has left university and started working.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage or alliance is a partnership, a joining of two.

clue.text: Give out everything, Genesis to Malachi initially

parts.note: all means everything
Genesis to Malachi spans the Old Testament, whose initials are O and T

explanation.surface: Someone told to hand out the whole Bible, from first book to last.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis is the first book and Malachi the last of the Old Testament in Christian Bibles.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute shares or portions is to give them out.

clue.text: Out of bed, terribly tired and optimistic

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
beat is informal for exhausted

explanation.surface: Somebody up and about, exhausted yet cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' looks like an anagram signal, but here it just intensifies 'tired'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerful, positive mood is described as upbeat, hopeful about things.

clue.text: Uninvited visitor at home, tons more disrespectful

parts.note: someone at home is in
T is the abbreviation for ton(s)
ruder means more impolite

explanation.surface: An unwelcome guest who, once indoors, becomes much ruder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters a place without permission is an unwelcome caller.

clue.text: Imprisonment of one contrarian upset about Church of England

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the church abbreviation
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A contrarian, angry with the established church, ends up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the contrarian's letters into NCARRATION, which 'about' wraps round the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Being locked up in jail is the state of imprisonment; the word comes from Latin carcer, prison.

clue.text: Church voiced English hymn tune

parts.note: something oral is spoken, voiced rather than written

explanation.surface: A congregation sings an English hymn tune aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voiced' is not a homophone signal here; it means spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately harmonised hymn melody, as in Lutheran worship, is a chorale.

clue.text: A quiet set of church bells give enjoyment

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a peal is a set of bells, or the sound they ring

explanation.surface: Gentle church bells bring pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that appeals to you pleases you, so to appeal is to delight or give pleasure.

clue.text: Shower party — much they stripped off

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: both words have their outer letters peeled off, leaving the middles

explanation.surface: At a party, many guests undressed and took a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped off' leaves UC from MUCH and HE from THEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet of water directed at the body for washing is a kind of shower.

clue.text: Credit fool with no intelligence

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of being a brainless fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Grossly stupid or insensitive behaviour is called crass, showing no thought.

clue.text: Sheets purchased initially before copier?

indicators.note: the first letter comes before the copier
takes just the first letter of the word it follows

parts.note: an aper is one who apes, or copies; the question mark flags this unusual sense

explanation.surface: Buying sheets of paper before using the photocopier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copier' looks like an office machine, but it means someone who apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper comes in sheets, so the material is defined by its form.

clue.text: Severely criticise the Spanish car bodywork

parts.note: critics pan a show they hate
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Slating the Spanish make of car for its bodywork.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a car's body shell is a body panel.

clue.text: See son with cannabis

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Catching one's son with marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, to see it.

clue.text: Public square in La Paz rebuilt

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A public square in the Bolivian city has been reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is the Spanish word, borrowed into English, for an open town square.

clue.text: Came to know Shakespeare's king Edward

parts.note: King Lear is the title king of a Shakespeare tragedy
Ned is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Getting acquainted with Shakespeare's King Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To have acquired knowledge of something is to have found it out, past tense of learn.

clue.text: Time to allay the fears of losing second prize

indicators.note: the soothing word loses one of its letters

parts.note: to reassure someone is to calm their fears

explanation.surface: It's time to calm people's worries about not winning second place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes one S out of REASSURE, leaving REASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to prize something is to value it highly, cherish it.

clue.text: Rules about banning European insinuation

indicators.note: turned about means turned round, so the letters run backwards
the abbreviation for European is barred, taken out

explanation.surface: Rules that exclude Europeans amount to a slight on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RULES round to SELUR, and 'banning' drops its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A disparaging hint or smear against someone's character is an aspersion of that kind.
